questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency $20MHz$ propagates in free space along $x$-direction. At a particular space and time $\overset{→}{E} = 6 . 6\overset{^}{j}Vm^{- 1}$. What is $\overset{→}{B}$ at this point?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that&

& $\overset{→}{E} = 6 . 6\overset{^}{j} ( Vm^{- 1} )$.

The relation between the electric, magnetic field and speed of light is~$\overset{→}{E} \times \overset{→}{B} = \overset{→}{c}$.

Clearly, $\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0} ( \overset{^}{k} )$

Using the relation,
~ ~ ~$c{B}_{0} = E$
$⇒ {B}_{0} = \left(\dfrac{E}{c}\right) = \dfrac{6 . 6}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = 2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 8}T$

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is represented by the electric filed $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{n}\sin \left[\omegat + \left(6y - 8z\right)\right] .$ Taking unit vectors in $x, y$ and $z$ directions to be $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{k},$ the directions of propogations $\overset{^}{s},$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The standard equation of electromagnetic wave& $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{n}\sin \left[\omegat -k\overset{^}{x}\right]$

here~$\overset{^}{x}$represents the direction of propagation wave.

On comparing the given equation with the standard~equation, the direction of propagation is along line $- 6y + 8z$ . Thus, unit vector along the direction of propagation is,
$\overset{^}{s} = \dfrac{- 6\overset{^}{j} + 8\overset{^}{k}}{10} = - \dfrac{3}{5}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{4}{5}\overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given by $E = 56 . 5sin\omega\left(\dfrac{t - x}{c}\right){NC}^{- 1}$. Find the intensity of the wave if it is propagating along $x$-axis in the free space. (Given~${ϵ}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}$)&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, $E = 56 . 5sin\omega\left(\dfrac{t - x}{c}\right)NC^{- 1}$

Comparing~it with the general equation of electromagnetic wave,~

$E = {E}_{0}\sin \left(\omegat -kx\right)$

We have,~${E}_{0} = 56 . 5NC^{- 1}$

So, the intensity will be $I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}_{0}^{2}$c$

=\dfrac{1}{2} \times$8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12} \times \left(56 . 5\right)2 \times3 \times {10}^{8}$

$= 4 . 24Wm^{- 2}

$

questions.q: An object is placed in a medium of refractive index $3$. An electromagnetic wave of intensity $6 \times {10}^{8}Wm^{- 2}$ falls normally on the object and it is absorbed completely. The radiation pressure on the object would be (speed of light in free space $= 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the radiation pressure is given by

$P = \dfrac{I}{v} . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, the velocity of the electromagnetic wave can be expressed as

$\mu = $\dfrac{c}{v} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

$\begin{cases}P & = & \dfrac{I \cdot \mu}{c}\\ & = & \dfrac{6 \times {10}^{8} \times 3}{3 \times {10}^{8}}\\ & = & 6Nm^{- 2}\end{cases}$$

questions.q: A point source of $100W$ emits light with $5 %$ efficiency. At a distance of $5m$ from the source, the intensity produced by the electric field component is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total power emitted& $= 100 \times \dfrac{5}{100} = 5W$

Now intensity due to electric field will be half of the total intensity. Therefore,

${I}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{power}{area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{5}{4\pi \times {5}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{40\pi}\dfrac{W}{m2}$

questions.q: The energy associated with electric field is  \left({U}_{E}\right)$ and with magnetic field is  \left({U}_{B}\right)$ for an electromagnetic wave in free space. Then:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average energy density of electric field is given by

${u}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}ε{E0}^{2}$

Here,~${E}_{0}$~is the maximum value of electric field.

The average energy density of magnetic field is given~by

${u}_{B} = \dfrac{{B}_{0}2}{2\mu}$

Here,~${B}_{0}$~is the maximum value of magnetic field.

The speed of light is given by~$c^{2} = \dfrac{1}{\muε}$

Also,~${E}_{0} = c{B}_{0}$

So,~${u}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2c^{2}\mu}\left(c{B}_{0}\right)2 = \dfrac{{B}_{0}2}{2\mu} = {u}_{B}$

As the energy density of electric field and magnetic field are equal, the energy associated for equal volume will also be equal.

questions.q: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by& $\overset{→}{B} = 2 \times {10}^{- 8}\sin \left(0 . 5 \times {10}^{3}x + 1 . 5 \times {10}^{11}t\right)\overset{^}{j}T$. The amplitude of the electric field would be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The ratio of electric field amplitude to the magnetic field amplitude of an electromagnetic wave is equal to the speed of light in the medium. Therefore,

$c = \dfrac{E0}{B0} ⇒ {E}_{0} = c{B}_{0}$

$⇒ {E}_{0} = 3 \times {10}^{8} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 8}$

$⇒ {E}_{0} = 6Vm^{- 1}$

According to the given equation~$\overset{→}{B} = 2 \times {10}^{- 8}\sin \left(0 . 5 \times {10}^{3}x + 1 . 5 \times {10}^{11}t\right)\overset{^}{j}T$~the wave travels in~$x$~direction. As electric field and magnetic field vibrate perpendicular to the velocity of light, electric field can not be along~$x$& axis.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency $35MHz$ travels in free space along the $X$-direction. At a particular point (in space and time) $\overset{→}{E} = 9 . 6\overset{^}{j}Vm^{- 1}$. The value of magnetic field at this point is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At every instant, the ratio of the magnitude of the electric field to the magnitude of the magnetic field in an electromagnetic wave equals the speed of light.

Therefore, $\dfrac{E}{B} = c$

$⇒ \dfrac{E}{B} = 3 \times {10}^{8}$

$⇒ B = \dfrac{E}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = \dfrac{9 . 6}{3 \times {10}^{8}}$

$⇒ B = 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 8}T$

Now, direction of magnetic field can be calculated as

$\overset{^}{B} = \overset{^}{v} \times \overset{^}{E}$

$= \overset{^}{i} \times \overset{^}{j} = \overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{→}{B} = 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 8}\overset{^}{k}T$

questions.q: The electric fields of two plane electromagnetic plane waves in vacuum are given by $\overset{→}{{E}_{1}} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{j}\cos \left(\omegat -kx\right)$ and $\overset{→}{{E}_{2}} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{k}\cos \left(\omegat -ky\right)$ At $t = 0,$ a particle of charge $q$ is at origin with a velocity $\overset{→}{v} = 08c\overset{^}{j}$ ( $c$ is the speed of light in vaccum). The instantaneous force experienced by the particle is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Magnetic field vectors associated with this electromagnetic wave are given by
${\overset{→}{B}}_{1} = \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{c}\overset{^}{k}\cos \left(kx - \omegat\right)$ & ${\overset{→}{B}}_{2} = $\dfrac{{E}_{0}}{c}\overset{^}{i}$\cos \left(ky - \omegat\right)$
$\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{E} + q \left(\overset{→}{V} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)
=q\left({\overset{→}{E}}_{1} + {\overset{→}{E}}_{2}\right) +$q \left(\overset{→}{V} \times \left({\overset{→}{B}}_{1} + {\overset{→}{B}}_{2}\right)\right)$
By putting the value of ${\overset{→}{E}}_{1}, {\overset{→}{E}}_{2}, {\overset{→}{B}}_{1} & {\overset{→}{B}}_{2}$
The net Lorentz force on the charged particles is
$\overset{→}{F} = q{E}_{0}\left[0.8\cos \left(kx - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + \cos \left(ky - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{j} + 0.2\cos \left(ky - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{k}\right]$
At $t = 0$ and at $x = y = 0$
$\overset{→}{F} = q{E}_{0} \left[0.8\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 0.2\overset{^}{k}\right]$

In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field vector and magnetic field vector are given as $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}$~and $\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{k}$, respectively. The direction of
propagation of electromagnetic wave is along:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Direction of propagation $= \overset{→}{E} \times \overset{→}{B} = \overset{^}{i} \times \overset{^}{k} = - \overset{^}{j}$.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave, at an instant and at a particular position, the electric field is along the negative z-axis and magnetic field is along the positive x-axis. Then the direction of propagation of electromagnetic wave is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along& $\overset{→}{E} \times \overset{→}{B}$

Thus,

$\overset{→}{n} = E \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right) \timesB \left(\overset{^}{i}\right)

Therefore,

$\overset{^}{n} = - \overset{^}{k} $\times \overset{^}{i} = - \overset{^}{j}

$

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{BC} \Rightarrow 60=\mathrm{B} \times 3 \times 10^8\Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=2 \times 10^{-7}$
Also $\quad $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{f}$ \lambda$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3 \times 10^8=\mathrm{f} \times 4 \times 10^{-3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=\frac{3}{4} \times 10^{11} \\ & \Rightarrow \omega=2 \pi \mathrm{f}=\frac{3}{4} \times 2 \pi \times 10^{11} \\ & \Rightarrow \omega=\frac{\pi}{2} \times 10^3 \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$\Rightarrow \quad$ Electric field $\Rightarrow y$ direction
Propagation $\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}$ direction
Magnetic field $\Rightarrow \mathrm{z}$-direction

questions.q: Sun light falls normally on a surface of area $36{cm}^{2}$ and exerts an average force of $7 . 2 \times {10}^{- 9}N$~within a time period of $20$ minutes. Considering a case of complete absorption, the energy flux of incident light is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The radiation pressure in case of complete absorption is given by,

$P = \dfrac{I}{c}$.

Therefore, the force will be,

$F = \dfrac{I}{c} \times A ⇒ I = \dfrac{Fc}{A}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{7 . 2 \times {10}^{- 9} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{36 \times {10}^{- 4}} = 600Wm^{- 2} ⇒ I = 0 . 06W{cm}^{- 2}$

questions.q:
A beam of light travelling along $X$-axis is described by the electric field ${E}_{y} = 900sin\omega \left($t - $\dfrac{x}{c}\right). The ratio of electric force to magnetic force on a charge $q$~moving along $Y$-axis with a speed of $3 $\times {10}^{7}$ms^{- 1}$ will be :

[Given speed of light $= 3 $\times {10}^{8}$ms^{- 1}$ \text{ and } ]

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,& ${E}_{y} = 900\sin \left(\omegat - \dfrac{\omegax}{c}\right)

Here,~${E}_{0} = 900$

Electric field and electric force are related as~${F}_{E} = q{E}_{0}$

Magnetic force of a moving charge is given by~${F}_{B} = qv{B}_{0}$

Thus, the ratio~\dfrac{FE}{FB} = \dfrac{E0}{v{B}_{0}}

Using relation between magnetic and electric field, we have

\dfrac{FE}{FB} = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{3 \times {10}^{7}} =$10: 1$

$

questions.q: The ratio of average electric energy density and total average energy density of electromagnetic wave is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Average electric energy density is stated& as& ${u}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2}$

Total average energy density~$U = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2{μ}_{0}}B^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2{μ}_{0}}\dfrac{E2}{c2}$~ ~ (As~$B = \dfrac{E}{c}$)

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2{μ}_{0}}E^{2}{ε}_{0}{μ}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}E^{2}{ε}_{0} = {ε}_{0}E^{2}$

Hence, the ratio,~$\dfrac{uE}{U} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
